newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FORECAST-TNT seen reporting year loss.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FORECAST-TNT seen reporting year loss.

text.p: Australian transport group TNT Ltd is expected to report a pre-abnormal net loss after preference dividends of between A$4 million and A$22 million and for year to June 30, analysts said.
TNT reported a net profit before abnormals and after preference dividends of A$38.47 million in 1994/95.
Analysts have savagely cut their forecasts for TNT since the start of 1996. The average forecast for TNT pre-abnormal net profit after preference dividends was about A$60 million.
A spokesman for BZW Investment Management said BZW's Barcep survey of transport analysts showed a concensus forecast pre-abnormal, post-tax and preference dividends loss of A$15 million for TNT.

In July, TNT said it expected 1995/96 earnings to be below the previous year, with its operating results to be about break even. The company said trading conditions had deteriorated during its third quarter.
"It looks like being another disappointing year for the company which could a review of the company's management," one Sydney based analyst said.
"I have revised down my forecast even further since July."
Contributing to the expected loss is Ansett Airlines Ltd
Last month, News Corp said the airline made a loss in the year to June 30, 1996 but did not quantify the result.
Earlier on Monday Air New Zealand Ltd AIRa.NZ said it would acquire TNT's 50 percent stake in Ansett for a total of A$475 million.
The purchase is conditional on the consent of the Australian Treasurer following an application to the Foreign Investment Review Board.
TNT shares were two cents weaker at A$1.46.
Its shares have fallen about 21 percent since June 30, 1995.
